instruction: You are a strategic corporate innovation advisor. Analyse the company profile and survey responses, then respond ONLY with a valid JSON object containing maturity_score, opportunities, next_steps, and key_weaknesses.

answers.companyDescription: Element Group is an engineering design consultancy providing specialized structural, MEP, and sustainability consulting for large-scale commercial and infrastructure projects. Our team of 60 engineers leverages Revit, AutoCAD, and IES VE for sophisticated building performance simulations, positioning us as a technical partner to developers and government agencies.
answers.pastInitiatives: We installed IoT sensors on 40% of our production equipment to monitor utilization and predict failures. The pilot showed a 15% reduction in unplanned downtime on instrumented machines, demonstrating early success with operational technology integration. We now have a business case approved for full fleet rollout, but procurement and integration with our legacy maintenance system are proving more complex than anticipated.
answers.strategicGoals: Our board has set an ambitious revenue target of reaching €50M ARR within 5 years from our current base. This requires us to expand our addressable market, potentially pivot pricing models from one-time project fees to recurring performance services, and build a repeatable enterprise sales motion. We need to identify the highest-leverage growth levers without overextending our cash runway.
answers.additionalContext: The company is currently facing competition from both larger integrated design firms and nimble boutique sustainability consultancies. Internal friction exists between the highly specialized technical teams focused on deep problem-solving and the need for scalable, standardized service delivery systems.
answers.teamSize: Our R&D function consists of 10-12 engineers organized into two squads: one focused on core product innovation and one on exploratory/new business model prototyping. We also have 2 dedicated data engineers building our analytics infrastructure. Innovation projects follow a lean startup methodology with clear go/no-go criteria at 3-month checkpoints.

opportunities.title: Process Automation via Workflow Integration
opportunities.rationale: Implementing RPA and AI tools to automate repetitive tasks like preliminary design checks or compliance reporting will immediately improve efficiency in our high-volume engineering workflow. This incremental step addresses current bottlenecks identified between core operations and innovation efforts.

first_actions: Conduct a full process mapping exercise for the MEP design phase.
Pilot an AI tool integration for initial code compliance checks.
execution_plan.success_metric: 30% reduction in time spent on administrative design tasks within 6 months.
milestones: Q1: Automated compliance check pilot complete.
Q2: Full department rollout of standard workflow templates.

opportunities.title: Productized Sustainability Consulting Service
opportunities.rationale: Given the high regulatory pressure and customer feedback on sustainability, Element Group should pivot from project-based consulting to offering standardized, modular 'Sustainability Performance Packages' sold as recurring SaaS or subscription services. This radical shift aligns with the strategic goal of creating a repeatable enterprise sales motion.

first_actions: Identify three high-demand sustainability niches (e.g., net-zero readiness for commercial real estate).
Develop a minimum viable product (MVP) service module with clear pricing tiers.
resources_needed: Investment in proprietary performance modeling software licenses.
execution_plan.success_metric: Achieve $2M ARR from subscription-based sustainability services within 18 months.
milestones: Q3: MVP service launched and priced for pilot clients.
Q4: Secure first three anchor recurring revenue contracts.

next_steps.action: Establish a cross-functional Innovation Steering Committee focused solely on defining and prioritizing 'Growth' vectors.
Initiate a feasibility study to determine the technical debt and integration cost associated with standardizing core consulting workflows.

key_weaknesses: Inconsistent innovation process leading to siloed digital maturity levels across engineering teams.
Over-reliance on manual, spreadsheet-based workflows which severely limits scalability and increases human error risk.
Reactive rather than proactive approach to market shifts due to the existing formal committee decision-making structure.
High competitive pressure makes long-term strategic planning difficult without radical pivots.
